newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ruggiero says NGOs "bridge" to future for trade.
newsitem.headline: Ruggiero says NGOs "bridge" to future for trade.

text.p: World Trade Organisation (WTO) director-general Renato Ruggiero said on Sunday non-governmental organisations (NGOs) were important to the future of free trade.
Ruggiero was speaking to delegates from some 150 NGOs from more than 35 countries on the eve of the opening of the WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore.
"Your presence is important because you are a bridge, an essential link between what we are trying to accomplish in the WTO and what the public expects us to accomplish," he said.
He added that the momentum for trade liberalisation was becoming more dependent on public support, and NGOs would find themselves in a middle role between the public and governments.
"Trade has moved to the center of public debate all over the world because trade is so central to people's lives, their jobs, living standards, their economic security," Ruggiero.
He urged the NGO community to work on bringing globalisation benefits to all countries, stressing more had to be done to bring Least Developed Countries (LLDCs) into the fold.

He said NGOs could facilitate that transition because they represented not just one sector, or one point of view, but a global community of interests, from business to consumers, labour, academia and the environment.
"To obtain the maximum benefit from globalisation we will need that kind of trans-national and multi-disciplinary perspective you provide," Ruggiero said.
He noted one example of such efforts was work with international companies to extend the reach of technical co-operation to less developed countries.
